thread:
alex_w: heads up — dashboard alert: spike in fncall schema rejections from the last SDK rollout. +1200 rejects in 10m. anyone own the mapping between route_id and billing route?

maria_g: saw that too. console shows most events mapped to `fallback:degen` route even when clients set `route_id` in header.

cheng_l: can you paste a sample payload and the validator error?

alex_w: here — payload and error from logs:

```
REQUEST: {"user_id":"u-123", "action":"generate_report", "details": {"format":"pdf","pages":10}}
VALIDATOR ERROR: fncall_schema: required property 'tool_args' missing (at /details)
```

jess: interesting — our SDK used to inject `tool_args` wrapper for some legacy clients but the new shim removed it. some clients still send old shape (no wrapper) and validator now rejects strictly.

tim_p: is that the strict validate canary turned on? I thought it was only in eu-west slice.

alex_w: can confirm canary rolled to 20% yesterday. rollout note: https://go/internal/rollouts/3342 (internal only).

maria_g: telemetry question — are we sampling these rejects at full fidelity? console shows counts but not sample payloads. ops-bot: debug-sampling is OFF for `validation.rejects` by default.

cheng_l: we need two quick things: 1) ensure samples are stored for the last hour for triage, 2) check routing attribution (why `route_id` get overridden).

jess: for (1) we can flip the sampling override for this rule — small retention cost. I can deploy a patch to the sampler pipeline.

maria_g: for (2) my hunch: the runtime fallback policy runs *after* header parsing and may rewrite route when capacity saturates. if the new SDK dropped `tool_args` the request may match a degenerate rule and get sent to degenerate route which strips headers.

tim_p: that sounds plausible. if the runtime reroutes before audit tagging, billing will see `fallback:degen`. we should add a `route_origin` tag set before any reroute. low-friction add.

alex_w: agree — add `route_origin=client` pre-reroute. then console can filter rejections by origin. can we do that short term?

jess: yes — two-line change in router, plus a migration to backfill last 24h? backfill not necessary right now — we'll start recording and then run a one-off query for historical fuzzy matches.

cheng_l: also propose we add a temporary permissive validator mode for this canary slice: treat missing `tool_args` as tolerated for 24-48h and emit `soft_reject` metric instead of hard reject. that will prevent customer-facing errors while we coordinate SDK patch.

maria_g: AV (product) gave thumbs up for permissive short window, as long as we surface degrades in console and tie to an action item for SDK roll.

tim_p: small caution: permissive mode still consumes quota if routed to degen? we need to ensure quota attribution is correct to avoid chargeback confusion. ops-bot: quota-routing currently uses final `route_id` at tokenization stage. adding `route_origin` tag won't change charge assignment without a follow-up change.

alex_w: okay action items:
- jess: flip sampling override for `validation.rejects` -> retain payloads for 1h (urgent)
- cheng_l: add `route_origin` tag pre-reroute and a short-lived metric `reroute_count_by_origin`
- jess + cheng_l: add permissive validator toggle for canary slice (24-48h)
- maria_g: coordinate with SDK owners and product + send customer comms if needed

jess: I'll open PRs for sampler and permissive toggle: https://go/internal/prs/9812

cheng_l: opening router PR for `route_origin` now. will mark default `route_origin=server` if shim absent.

maria_g: I'll create a console dashboard card that shows `validation.rejects` split by `route_origin` and `route_id`, and include link to samples.

tim_p: set up a retention alarm if rejects stay >5% for next 2h. ops-bot: alarm rule created (ID: alarm-7712).

alex_w: thanks — if anyone sees urgent customer hits ping me. otherwise let's reconvene in 2 hours with initial sampling data. :thumbsup:
